title: Elastic micro-shard hedging and cold-slice materialization for multitenant dashboard queries
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: High tail latency for tenant dashboard list queries when time-window scans hit cold slices or highly skewed tenants. Existing broad prefetch increases read amplification and cost for large orgs. Goal: Reduce p99/p999 for multi-tenant time-series dashboard queries while keeping read amplification and storage overhead bounded.
acceptance_criteria: p99 tail latency for 30s time-window dashboard queries reduced by >= 35% in staging compared to baseline
Average extra read amplification per query <= 1.5x versus baseline for heavy tenants
No more than 10% increase in storage for materialized cold-slices on average across tenants
Feature flag controlled rollout and automated rollback on error rate > 0.5%
End-to-end e2e tests for hedging logic and cold-slice materialization added to CI
implementation_notes: Introduce micro-shard concept: break per-tenant time windows into small immutable 'micro-slices' keyed by (tenant, timeframe-hash) to allow targeted materialization and eviction
Read path hedging: when primary slice read latency exceeds hedging threshold (configurable; default 120ms), issue a speculative read to a secondary replica or to a materialized cold-slice store

Cold-slice materialization: asynchronously compact and store infrequently accessed micro-slices in a fast-read column store (S3 + vectorized reads via Presto/Trino or RocksDB on hot nodes). Materialization rate limited by token bucket per-tenant to bound IO cost
Adaptive selector: runtime uses tenant access fingerprint (recent query frequency, size) to decide whether to materialize or serve from raw shards
Backpressure and circuit breaker: if materializer queue grows > 1000 tasks or error rate increases, disable materialization for the tenant for 10 minutes and fall back to baseline read path
Instrumentation: add trace spans for hedged read, materialize enqueue/dequeue, and final serve path. Tag traces with tenant and timeframe-hash for sampling and aggregation
Migration: gradually enable materialization for 5% of tenants by usage cohort, measure read amplification and storage; expand cohorts on success
Schema: add micro_slice metadata table with fields (tenant_id, timeframe_hash, materialized_at, size_bytes, last_accessed). Keep as separate service to avoid locking hot OLTP tables
metrics_and_benchmarks: Baseline staging results (2026-02-18): p99=1.02s, p999=2.42s for 30s window multi-tenant queries
Initial A/B on 50 tenants (2026-02-28): p95 improved 15%, p99 improved 28% but read amplification increased 1.9x for 3 tenants with bursting patterns
We will track: query_latency_pXX_by_tenant, materializer_queue_size, cold_slice_hit_rate, storage_change_pct_by_tenant, read_amplification_factor
Cost impact estimation: materialization expected to add ~0.6% storage + marginal read cost savings of 0.4% at global scale when enabled for 40% active tenants
roll_out_plan: Feature gated via console feature-flag 'micro_slice_materialization' and hedging config in runtime-config service
Phase 1 (Canary): Enable for 5% small tenants (low-QPS) for 2 days; validate latency, materializer stability, and storage growth
Phase 2 (Targeted): Expand to 20% including medium tenants; enable advanced adaptive selector; run canary traffic for 1 week
Phase 3 (Ramp): Gradually reach 60% by automated expansion if metrics within thresholds; open support docs and cost guide
Rollback: global toggle and per-tenant kill-switch; automatic rollback if error_rate > 0.5% or materializer queue sustained > threshold
